| [TERM-140](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-140.md) v4 | sloppy, of a parametric model at a point and for an observation design: its Fisher information spectrum, in a declared chart, spreads evenly over many decades with no gap that separates the parameter combinations that matter from those that do not, along eigenvectors skewed from the bare parameter axes; a graded property, distinct from ill-conditioning and from singularity | At the owner's suggestion of 2026-11-21, after the filing of the exchange "Rich Get Richer Power Laws": "a TERM for the mathematical (information geometric?) sense of 'sloppy' might be merited". The record used the word in that sense in several entries ([TERM-135](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-135.md), [TERM-137](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-137.md), [CLAIM-813](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-813.md), [CLAIM-820](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-820.md), [CLAIM-812](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-812.md)) and in its readings of sloppy spectra ([THEORY-774](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-774.md), [THEORY-777](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-777.md)), without defining it. A model is sloppy, at a parameter point and for a given observation design, when the eigenvalues of its Fisher information, in a declared chart (conventionally the logarithms of its bare parameters), spread evenly over many decades, no gap among them marks off the combinations that matter from those that do not, and the eigenvectors are skewed from the bare parameter axes. The term separates this from three neighbours: ill-conditioning (one ratio, which a single gap can produce), singularity (a zero eigenvalue on a stratum), and the hyperribbon (the chart-free shape of the predictions, [TERM-135](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-135.md)). It says nothing of the law by which the spectrum falls. Its job is to let the record's entries on sloppiness, singular learning and effective dimension say which of these they mean. The source of the concept is Sethna and colleagues: LIT-2977, LIT-3009 and LIT-2994, read on 2026-11-21 (THEORY-2156, THEORY-2155, THEORY-2154), and the survey LIT-2999, read the same day (THEORY-2165). They define sloppiness by example, by an eigenvalue spread "evenly spaced in their logarithm" and by skew from the bare axes, and put its chart-free content in the widths of the model manifold; versions 2 and 3 record what they say. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
